metadata.title: PCR-001: Standard PCR
metadata.purpose: Amplify a defined DNA segment from plasmid DNA, genomic DNA, cDNA, or purified PCR product using endpoint PCR. This standalone SOP is written for a 50 uL Taq-style reaction and can be scaled or adapted to high-fidelity polymerases by following enzyme-specific instructions.
metadata.scope: Standalone detailed external-reference SOP draft for a 50 uL Taq-style endpoint PCR reaction. Before operational use, review against the exact reagent, instrument, plate/tube format, biosafety level, waste rules, and institutional SOPs used by the lab.
beforeYouBegin: Use a clean pre-PCR workspace, fresh gloves, aerosol-resistant tips, and dedicated pre-PCR pipettes where possible.
Keep enzymes, master mixes, primers, probes, dNTPs, and template on ice unless the manufacturer explicitly permits room-temperature setup.
Prepare a master mix for all shared components and add 5-10% excess volume for pipetting loss.
Add template last. For contamination-sensitive assays, load no-template controls last and keep amplified DNA away from setup areas.
Briefly centrifuge tubes or plates before cycling so liquid is collected at the bottom and bubbles are removed.
Record template ID, primer/probe ID, reagent lot, cycling program, thermal cycler or qPCR instrument ID, expected product size, and deviations.

materials.name: Template DNA
materials.specification: plasmid, genomic DNA, cDNA, purified amplicon, or validated control template

materials.name: Thin-wall PCR tubes or PCR plate

equipment.name: Microcentrifuge
equipment.settings: Briefly spin to collect liquid at tube/plate bottom and remove bubbles

tables.title: Primer design checklist
rows: Longer primers may be required for cloning tails; calculate Tm from the annealing region.
Avoid very low GC content, long single-base runs, and strong hairpins.
Use one consistent Tm calculator for both primers.
Avoid 3 prime complementarity between primers; a weak GC clamp can help specificity.
Routine endpoint PCR is commonly 100 bp to several kb; long products need enzyme-specific optimization.

tables.title: Example 50 uL reaction setup
rows: Plasmid: 1-10 ng; genomic DNA: 10-500 ng; adjust by assay.

tables.title: Cycling program
rows: Denature template and activate enzyme if applicable.
Optimize by gradient if weak or nonspecific.

tables.title: Run Record Template
rows: Primer/probe IDs and sequences or inventory references
Master mix/enzyme name, catalog, lot, and expiration
Thermal cycler or qPCR instrument ID
Cycling program name and exact settings
Result file, Cq export, gel image, or sequencing confirmation
tables.note: Complete this record whenever the protocol is run or adapted into an internal SOP.

steps.action: Thaw buffer, dNTPs, primers, water, and template on ice. Mix compatible reagents gently and briefly spin down.
Label tubes or plate wells. Include an NTC and a positive control before starting the run.
Calculate master mix volumes for all shared components except template. Add 5-10% overage.
Add water, buffer, dNTPs, shared primers if applicable, and polymerase to the master mix. Mix gently without foaming.
Dispense master mix into tubes/wells. Add template DNA last. Add nuclease-free water instead of template to the NTC.
steps.criticalNotes: Add template DNA last. Add nuclease-free water instead of template to the NTC.

steps.action: Seal tubes/plate, briefly centrifuge, and place in the thermal cycler.
Run the cycling program below or the enzyme-specific program.

parameters.rawText: Initial denaturation 94-98 deg C 2 min; Denaturation 94-98 deg C 30 sec
Annealing Tm - 3 to 5 deg C 20-30 sec
Extension 72 deg C 30-60 sec/kb; Final extension 72 deg C 5 min

repeat.notes: The source specifies 25-35 cycles for denaturation, annealing, and extension steps.

steps.action: Analyze 2-5 uL product on agarose gel with a ladder covering the expected product size.
Accept a run when the expected sample band appears, the positive control works, and the NTC has no target-size band.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Expected sample band appears at the correct size.
The NTC has no target-size band.

steps.action: If the product will be cloned or sequenced, purify by PCR cleanup or gel extraction depending on specificity.

controls.name: No-template control (NTC)
controls.description: Detect reagent, water, primer, or setup contamination.
controls.acceptance: No target-size endpoint PCR band; for qPCR, no target-like amplification or target-like melt peak.

controls.name: Positive control
controls.description: Verify that the assay, master mix, template handling, cycling program, and detection method work.
controls.acceptance: Expected band or expected Cq/melt/probe signal.

controls.name: Replicates
controls.acceptance: Endpoint PCR: consistent band pattern. qPCR: replicate SD commonly <= 0.3 Cq for established assays, unless assay-specific limits differ.

controls.name: Run record
controls.description: Make the protocol auditable and reproducible.
controls.acceptance: Complete sample map, reagent lots, program, instrument, and result file or gel image.

expectedOutputs: Expected sample band appears at the correct size on agarose gel.
Positive control shows expected band or expected Cq/melt/probe signal.
No-template control has no target-size endpoint PCR band; for qPCR, no target-like amplification or target-like melt peak.
If the product will be cloned or sequenced, purified PCR product by PCR cleanup or gel extraction depending on specificity.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong annealing temperature, missing component, degraded template, inhibitors, insufficient extension.
troubleshooting.solution: Verify setup map; lower annealing or run gradient; increase extension; dilute template to reduce inhibitors; use fresh enzyme.

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing too low, excess template/primer, nonspecific primer binding.
troubleshooting.solution: Raise annealing temperature; reduce template or primer; use hot-start polymerase; redesign primers.

troubleshooting.cause: Overcycling, degraded template, nonspecific amplification, overloaded gel.
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce cycles; improve template; optimize annealing; load less product.

troubleshooting.cause: Primer complementarity or high primer concentration.
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce primer to 0.2-0.3 uM or redesign primers.

safety: Use a clean pre-PCR workspace, fresh gloves, aerosol-resistant tips, and dedicated pre-PCR pipettes where possible.
Add template last. For contamination-sensitive assays, load no-template controls last and keep amplified DNA away from setup areas.
Before operational use, review against the exact reagent, instrument, plate/tube format, biosafety level, waste rules, and institutional SOPs used by the lab.
Review when reagent, instrument, cycling program, analysis method, or safety requirement changes.
No dedicated safety section in source PDF; the items above are extracted from the general setup rules and document disclaimer. Review against institutional safety requirements before bench use.
